opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E049 (John Rodriguez) is a full-time Analyst. Full-time employees may have up to write access, so the requested write access to Source Code is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E049 (John Rodriguez) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training may have at most read access. Requested write exceeds this, so recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent verified in their database that E049 (John Rodriguez) is a contractor with basic security training, which is the relevant security record for Source Code access. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; with basic training the maximum is read. The requested write access exceeds this maximum, so I grant read.

- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
